Rating is one over the square root of how likely your card was — six traits, six published frequencies, one formula, checkable on paper. To beat is empirical: 30 pulls have been made and r of them beat rank r, so about one pull in 30/r takes that seat — which is why rank 10 is roughly ten times cheaper to take than rank 1. Reach is clicks that card has sent to the product’s site. The bar is log-scaled: on a linear axis the whole tail below rank 12 would be invisible. The crown is pull-only — the pity ladder tops out at Legendary and the shop caps at Epic, so money can buy you into contention and never buys first place. The rest of the wave is counted and priced at every board, measured — median top bid $5, 4 of 94 never paid a dollar — and the two mechanics are put side by side at OutRip vs outbid.lol.
